Please describe your model/approach in detail.
column2: We implemented a two-tier hybrid computational genomics pipeline combining hypothesis-driven targeted candidate panel interrogation with an unbiased genome-wide genic sweep: 1) Targeted branch: curated 7 OMIM-confirmed MVA genes (BUB1B, CEP57, TRIP13, CENATAC, SLF2, SMC5, MAD1L1) using MANE Select coordinates on GRCh38. Extracted 1,073 variants from the proband VCF and annotated via Ensembl VEP (gnomAD v4 AF, ClinVar, SIFT/PolyPhen). 2) Global branch: extracted all ~20,000 human gene bodies (±20bp for splice junctions) from Ensembl Release 110 GTF (~5M variants) and performed high-throughput multi-threaded annotation via local Docker VEP with the Phenotypes plugin. 3) Prioritization & Scoring: filtered for rarity (gnomAD AF < 0.01) and severe consequences (stop-gained, frameshift, splice donor/acceptor, deleterious missense). Weighted phenotype scores were applied based on the proband's clinical presentation (rhabdomyosarcoma, nephrocalcinosis, IUGR, prematurity, recurrent miscarriages). 4) Genotype Quality Control: re-integrated GATK call metrics, requiring FILTER=PASS, DP >= 10, alt AD >= 1, and non-reference genotype. 5) Recessive Pairing Engine & Ranking: combined consensus hits across branches, grouped heterozygous variants per gene into compound heterozygous pairs, and calibrated EPCR scores into [0.05, 1.0] for the top 10 ranked submissions.

column1: Provide a method abstract (up to 500 words). Please include strengths and limitations of your method as well as methodological detail.
column2: Mosaic Variegated Aneuploidy (MVA) is an ultrarare disorder of the mitotic spindle assembly checkpoint (SAC). Identifying causal variants from whole genome sequencing requires high sensitivity to capture rare, compound heterozygous events while eliminating millions of benign polymorphisms. We developed an automated, reproducible two-tier genomics pipeline that merges targeted gene interrogation (OMIM MVA1–MVA7) with an unbiased genome-wide genic scan across >20,000 genes. Genomic variants from the proband's WGS VCF (GRCh38) were annotated using Ensembl VEP (release 110.1) for molecular consequence severity, gnomAD v4 rarity (<1%), in silico pathogenicity (SIFT, PolyPhen), and ClinVar assertions. Hits were matched against the proband’s clinical phenotype (rhabdomyosarcoma, nephrocalcinosis, IUGR, and parental recurrent miscarriages) using a weighted HPO matrix. To model autosomal recessive inheritance, the pipeline re-integrated GATK genotype metrics (FILTER=PASS, DP >= 10, alt AD >= 1) and executed a gene-level pairing algorithm to detect compound heterozygous pairs. The pipeline surfaced a compound heterozygous mutation in BUB1B (MVA1) as the top causal candidate (EPCR = 1.0), comprising a ClinVar-confirmed pathogenic nonsense mutation (chr15:40209701 T>G, stop-gained) and a novel deleterious missense mutation (chr15:40220612 T>G). BUB1B encodes BubR1, a master regulator of chromosome segregation whose loss directly causes rhabdomyosarcoma and embryonic lethality. Strengths: rapid execution (<10 min), 100% automated reproducibility, dual targeted/global discovery, and explicit compound heterozygous modeling. Limitations: proband-only short-read data cannot computationally confirm variant phasing (trans vs. cis) without parental sequencing. Future work: integration of read-depth copy number (CNVkit) and B-allele frequency profiling.
